csl.abstract: Plant diseases cause annual crop losses of 20– 40%, threatening global food security. This paper presents a lightweight, mobile-deployable deep learning system for automated plant disease detection using transfer learning with MobileNetV2 on the PlantVillage dataset (54,303 RGB images, 38 classes across 14 crop species). Data augmentation techniques including rotation, flipping, and brightness variation were applied to improve robustness against real- field variability. The proposed model achieves 94.2% validation accuracy with a macro F1-score of 93.6%, outperforming classical baselines by over 6 percentage points, and attains 79.5% Top-1 accuracy on out-of-distribution field images. With 4.2M total parameters, the architecture is suitable for TensorFlow Lite conversion and real-time smartphone inference. The system enables early, accessible diagnosis without internet dependency, supporting precision agriculture and sustainable pest management.

title: Leakage-Proof Reliability-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Rice Leaf Disease Diagnosis

csl.abstract:
Yet, little is known about how well deep learning models for Bangladeshi rice leaf disease recognition perform when tested across different datasets, leaving an important question unanswered. Datasets differ in camera type, background, class set, and annotation standards; thus, high in-dataset accuracy on one of them does not guarantee high performance on the others. How much does the performance degrade? Is acquisition related? Which techniques can mitigate the effect?

We have normalized three Bangladesh-based datasets to a consistent class taxonomy, frozen the splits, and studied cross-dataset transfer performance via this models, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, and ResNet50 in six directions of ordered sharing classes. The in-dataset macro-F1 mean is 0.719, while the cross-dataset macro-F1 mean is 0.436 (mean gap 0.387). The strong data augmentation increases the cross-dataset macro-F1 mean from 0.436 to 0.503 (mean gap +0.070, Wilcoxon p≈0.0002 on 18 cells). Leave-one-dataset-out technique improves performance of the target model in only 3 out of 9 directions. Adaptive Batch Normalization improves results in only 5 out of 18 pairs. A ResNet50 bucket study attributes almost all the gains to the background randomization.

csl.abstract: Edge deployment of crop-leaf disease classifiersrequires compact INT8 models, but field photographs differsharply from the laboratory datasets used for training. Priorwork typically studies quantization or domain shift; few experiments measure whether the two effects interact. We traina MobileNetV2 classifier on a closed-set 27-class intersectionof PlantVillage, convert it to INT8 with TensorFlow Lite posttraining quantization (PTQ) calibrated on PlantVillage trainingimages only, and evaluate a 2 × 2 grid: float32 versus INT8 ×PlantVillage (in-domain) versus PlantDoc (out-of-domain, zeroshot).
